# @wweir/dsh-advisor
English | 简体中文
An automatic second opinion for DeepSeek Harness sessions.

On a configurable step rhythm, a **restricted sub-agent** re-reads the
Executor's recent work with r

ead-only tools. Concrete defects are recorded and
delivered to the Executor's inbox; when there is n

othing to point at, the
reviewer stays silent — silence is the normal outcome, not a failure.

The plugin never runs its own model loop: the review is a real child session,
so the host's turn/ste

p machine, tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation and
persistence apply to it unchanged.
## What it does for you

- **Catches hallucinations.** The reviewer reads the actual files (read-only):
changes claimed but n

ot made, APIs that do not exist, values never written.
The note points at the mismatch while the wor

k is fresh; delivery is
advisory, interrupting only as configured.
- **Keeps sessions on track.** At

most one review every N completed steps
(default 8), never concurrently — a step boundary that arri

ves mid-review
waits for the next cadence instead of stacking reviews. A step is one model
call plus

its tools, so one cadence covers work inside a long turn and work
spread across many short turns; `

everySteps: 0` turns automatic review off.
Drift is reported inside the running turn; idle sessions

can be woken by
severe findings (budgeted, severity-gated). Silence is reported as a result,
not an

error.
- **Bounded cost.** The reviewer's context is a compiled two-zone projection,
never a copy of

the Executor's. The prompt is capped by the operator's
`maxContextTokens` (64K by default) **and**

by the reviewer model's own
window: the host preamble, the model's output reserve and a margin are
s

ubtracted first, and a route that cannot hold even a minimal review is
refused with those numbers in

stead of overflowing into a host compaction.
The check is as good as the route's advertisement: a ro

ute that does not
report a window keeps the operator's cap, because that is the only number the
plug

in has.
The zone after the boundary carries the work since the last review that
concluded (a silent

or finding outcome), with its evidence graded by whether
the reviewer could re-obtain it: the Execut

or's visible claims travel, a tool
call keeps its name and arguments (shell commands capped at 600 c

haracters,
edits at 2,000), a file read or search the reviewer can repeat becomes its
path and size,

a shell result its status, a few failure lines and the tail,
and every other result — an edit, a to

ol error, `ls`, an MCP server, a
subagent, a job — keeps its text. Every message line is capped at 4

,000
characters. The zone before the boundary is a trace of
already-reviewed work, with tool-result

bodies omitted — and the prompt says
[该节后续省略]
## Why

Most advisor plugins hand the transcript to one extra LLM call and inject
whatever comes back. This

plugin makes the reviewer a **real child session with
its own read-only tools**, which buys four con

the reviewer a **real child session with
its own read-only tools**, which buys four concrete things:

- **It verifies instead of guessing.** The reviewer opens the files the
Executor actually touched, s

o a note points at a defect it looked at — not
a pattern inferred from a transcript summary, which i

s all a
transcript-only reviewer can ever offer.
- **The host's rules apply to the review itself.**

Turn/step accounting, the
tool pipeline, streaming, cancellation, persistence, and a real audit
trai

l: the review is a session you can inspect, and its cost is reported
usage, not an estimate.
- **Iso

lation is enforced, not promised.** One reviewer claim per process, a
read-only tool surface, a prot

ected-path guard deliberately stricter than
the upstream advisor (workspace-root private keys and `.

envrc` included),
and no shared context with the Executor.
- **Delivery is accounted.** A **follow-u

p** note counts as delivered only when
the host proves it was processed (that turn's model reply); a

n unconfirmed
note is requeued, never silently dropped. A note steered into a running turn
counts as

delivered at the hand-off. Repetition is suppressed by finding
identity plus similarity, with hash-

t the hand-off. Repetition is suppressed by finding
identity plus similarity, with hash-based mutes.
## Install

The package is a Cordis plugin (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`) and is
published on npm wit

h a provenance attestation, so it installs like any other
profile bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A development checkout can be linked instead (`dsh plugin … add /path/to/checkout`);
its deploy path
is described in `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

Then give it a model route. It is **disabled until a model is configured**, and
it never falls back
to the Executor's model:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A patch entry is **replaced, not merged**, per row id: an overlay that sets
only the extra instructi

ons drops the model route, so the row loads **disabled**;
it fails loudly, with a validation error,

only when the overlay also asks for
`enabled: true`.
## Behaviour worth knowing

- **Trigger** — one cadence: a completed *step*, i.e. one model call plus the
tools it ran. Steps ar

e the host's progress unit, so the same counter covers
work inside a long turn (which crosses no rep

ly boundary for dozens of steps)
and work spread across many short turns; there is no second, reply-

based
interval that could disagree with it. A review starts once `everySteps` steps
(default 8) have

accrued since the previous one finished. The cursor moves
when a review *finishes*, so a slow revie

w cannot chain into the next one; the
counter and cursor are absolute and persisted, so a reload con

tinues the
cadence instead of forgiving the steps that accrued since the last review. A
fresh sessio

n is first reviewed after a full cadence, not immediately. The
turn's final answer starts no review

of its own: the steps that produced it
already had their chance, so the tail of a session that stops

mid-cadence is
reviewed by the next steps that accrue. Sub-agent sessions (including the
review chi

ldren) are never reviewed. Turns this plugin opened itself are never
reviewed either.
- **Review chi

ld limits** — one review is one bounded attempt. It may run at
most five reads or searches; a furthe

r call is refused with the reason to
[该节后续省略]
